title: Mariam's First Business
author: Léxi
desc: Avec 20 000 francs et la recette de sa grand-mère, Mariam ouvre son petit commerce d'attiéké.

p: Mariam finished school at nineteen. She looked for a job for one year. Nothing. Every day, the same answer: "We'll call you." Nobody called.
One evening, her grandmother gave her an envelope. Inside, there were twenty thousand francs.
"It's all I have saved," said Grandma. "Don't wait for someone to give you a job, my child. Create your own."
"But what can I do with twenty thousand francs?"
Grandma laughed. "When I was young, I fed this whole family with a pot of attiéké and a lot of courage. My recipe is the best in Abobo. Everybody says it."
Mariam took a notebook. She wrote a plan, like they taught her at school.

*What do I sell? Attiéké with fried fish and a special sauce.*
*Who are my clients? Workers and students at lunchtime.*
*Where? In front of the big construction site near the university.*
*How much? Five hundred francs a plate.*
She calculated. The cassava, the fish, the oil, the onions, the charcoal, a table and a big umbrella: eighteen thousand francs. She had two thousand left.
The first morning, she woke up at four o'clock. She cooked with her grandmother. At eleven, she put her table in front of the construction site.
At noon, the workers came out. They walked past her. One, two, ten… nobody stopped.
The first day, Mariam sold three plates. The second day, five. On the third day, it rained, and she sold nothing. She threw the food away and cried.
"Maybe I'm not made for business," she told her grandmother.
Grandma was quiet. Then she asked: "Why didn't they buy?"
Mariam thought. "I don't know."
"Then go and ask them."

The next day, Mariam asked the workers. Their answers were simple. "Five hundred is too much for us at the end of the month." "We only have twenty minutes to eat. You're too slow." "We don't know you. Maybe your food is bad."
Mariam wrote everything in her notebook. Every bad answer was a good lesson.
Mariam changed her plan.

She made a small plate for three hundred francs and a big one for five hundred. She prepared the plates before noon, wrapped in paper, so the workers could take them in ten seconds. And on Monday, she gave free tasting spoons to everybody.
"Taste first, pay after!" she called with a big smile.
The workers tasted. Their eyes opened wide. "Hey! Who made this sauce?"
"My grandmother's secret recipe!"
That Monday, she sold forty plates. On Friday, she sold eighty. After one month, she needed help. She hired her cousin Awa.
One year later, Mariam has three tables in three places in Abidjan, and five employees. She calls her business *Grandma's Kitchen*.
She has a WhatsApp number for orders. She has a little logo: an old woman smiling with a big pot.
Every Sunday, she gives her grandmother an envelope. "It's your share, Grandma. You were my first investor."
Grandma laughs her big laugh. "Twenty thousand francs. The best investment of my life!"

In her notebook, on the first page, Mariam has written three rules:
*1. Start small, but start.*
*2. When it doesn't work, ask why.*
*3. Never forget who believed in you first.*
